messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The issue described is an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException occurring at Base64.encode at line 502 when repeatedly calling Base64InputStream.read() on an encoding stream. This is confirmed by the bug report and the test case reading the stream byte-by-byte multiple times.

Looking at the Base64InputStream.read() method, it delegates to Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int), which contains a while loop attempting to read bytes. Inside the loop, if there's no data available, the stream reads more from the underlying input stream, then either encodes or decodes based on the doEncode flag.

In the Base64.encode method, the exception occurs near line 502, which corresponds to the logic adding line separators after encoding 76 characters:
```
if (lineLength > 0 && lineLength <= currentLinePos) {
    System.arraycopy(lineSeparator, 0, buffer, pos, lineSeparator.length);
    pos += lineSeparator.length;
    currentLinePos = 0;
}
```

This code requires the buffer to have enough space for the line separator to be copied (System.arraycopy). The buffer is resized as needed in resizeBuffer() calls before encoding new input. However, in the encode method, a corner case can occur when the buffer is just barely large enough or when the resizing logic does not properly account for space needed to add line separators.

Additionally, the bug report says the exception happens after many successful reads (~10920), indicating the problem surfaces after large input or after several encoding cycles.

The Base64InputStream.read method also contains logic that calls base64.setInitialBuffer(b, offset, len) if the length of the read equals the entire buffer length being read into. This is potentially risky if setInitialBuffer does not correctly reset positional pointers or the state of Base64 encoding buffer.

In sum, the root cause appears to be a bug in the Base64.encode method when encoding large streams: the buffer size management or the position tracking (pos) is not robust enough to always allow safe copying of line separators, leading to an attempt to write past the end of the buffer and triggering ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

Additionally, Base64InputStream.read() repeatedly calls read(byte[], int, int) which calls encode, so the failure happens when multiple reads exhaust this faulty edge case.

The other bug report about Base64InputStream read(byte[]) returning zero is not directly relevant but suggests other errors in read handling.

Therefore, the fault is primarily in how Base64.encode manages its internal buffer and line separators during incremental encoding, causing array index errors under frequent read() calls in encoding mode.

Suggested locations for fix:
- The Base64.encode(byte[], int, int) method: buffer management and resizing logic around line separator insertion.
- Possibly Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int) and setInitialBuffer to ensure safe state setup before encoding.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

Base64.encode(byte[], int, int)
Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int)
Base64InputStream.read()
